title: Beautiful Arrangement II
description:
# Beautiful Arrangement II

Given two integers `n` and `k`, construct an array `answer` that contains every integer from `1` to `n` exactly once.

For `answer = [a1, a2, a3, ..., an]`, form the adjacent-difference array `[|a1 - a2|, |a2 - a3|, |a3 - a4|, ..., |a(n-1) - an|]`. This adjacent-difference array must contain exactly `k` distinct values.

Return any valid `answer`. Multiple valid arrays can exist, and the checker accepts any array that satisfies the permutation and distinct-difference conditions.

## Example 1:

**Input:** n = 3, k = 1
**Output:** [1,2,3]
**Explanation:** The adjacent differences are `[1,1]`, so there is exactly one distinct difference.

## Example 2:

**Input:** n = 3, k = 2
**Output:** [1,3,2]
**Explanation:** The adjacent differences are `[2,1]`, so there are exactly two distinct differences.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= k < n <= 10^4`.

solutions.name: Prefix Zigzag Construction
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the numbers `1..k+1` first. Alternate between the low and high ends of that range, then append the remaining numbers in increasing order.

## Key Insight

The first `k + 1` values create adjacent differences `k, k - 1, ..., 1`. Appending consecutive numbers only adds difference `1`, which is already present.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) besides the returned array

solutions.name: Increasing Prefix Then Tail Zigzag
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep the prefix `1..n-k-1` increasing, then zigzag through the final `k + 1` numbers by alternating the low and high ends of that tail range.

## Key Insight

The increasing prefix contributes only difference `1`. The tail zigzag contributes the larger differences `k, k - 1, ..., 2`, so the whole array has exactly `k` distinct differences.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) besides the returned array

solutions.name: Descending Difference Walk
solutions.description:
## Approach

Start at `1`, then walk by differences `k, k - 1, ..., 1`, alternating direction after every step. Append the unused larger values in increasing order.

## Key Insight

By choosing the difference size directly, the prefix guarantees every difference from `1` through `k` appears once. The remaining increasing suffix cannot introduce a new difference.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) besides the returned array

solutions.name: Global Extremes While Shrinking K
solutions.description:
## Approach

While more than one new difference is still needed, alternately take from the global low and high ends depending on the parity of the remaining difference count. Once only difference `1` remains, fill the rest in increasing order.

## Key Insight

Taking opposite extremes creates a large new adjacent difference each time. When the target count has been reduced to one, a consecutive suffix preserves exactly one remaining difference value.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) besides the returned array

tests.output: any valid permutation with 9999 distinct adjacent differences
